title: Cox Proportional Hazards Model
interviewAnswer: The Cox model relates covariates multiplicatively to hazard without specifying the baseline hazard shape. Coefficients are interpreted through hazard ratios, under the proportional-hazards assumption.
why: Cox Proportional Hazards Model appears frequently in data-science work because it connects mathematical assumptions to practical decisions, diagnostics and failure modes.
deepDive: The Cox model relates covariates multiplicatively to hazard without specifying the baseline hazard shape. Coefficients are interpreted through hazard ratios, under the proportional-hazards assumption. Check proportional hazards. Censoring assumptions still matter. A strong practitioner separates the modeling assumption from the estimation procedure, checks diagnostics rather than trusting a single score, and explains what would make the method inappropriate.
workedExample: A hazard ratio of 1.5 for a feature means 50% higher instantaneous event hazard at a given time, holding other covariates fixed.
commonMistakes: Applying the method without checking its assumptions or data-generating process.
Choosing it because it is familiar rather than comparing against an appropriate baseline.
followUps: What assumptions does Cox Proportional Hazards Model make?
How would you validate or debug Cox Proportional Hazards Model in practice?
production: In production, validate assumptions on real data, monitor the quantities that can drift, and keep a simple baseline so added complexity has a measurable reason to exist.
